lede: The biggest thing on the board this week is Mountain Village Town Council meeting Thursday to vote on a sale price appreciation cap for deed-restricted units — the kind of decision that determines whether affordable housing actually stays affordable or quietly slides away. Ouray County's Planning Commission also holds three public hearings Wednesday, including a full repeal of Section 16 of their land use code, which is the sort of wholesale change that reshapes future development decisions for years. Closer to home, Telluride's P&Z takes its first formal look at the school district's employee housing proposal, and HARC sits down with the Shandoka Lot redevelopment — two projects that will leave a mark on the west end of town.
